text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended marginally higher in quiet trade. Front-month May and August were the only sessions traded in the AA-dominated session, finishing at $308.50 and $307.00 per tonne respectively, up 50 and 40 cents. Raw sugar futures in New York closed slightly higher across the board in uneventful dealings. Front-month May ended near 11.00 cents/lb at 10.97 cents/lb, up 4 points from Thursday. July ended up 6 points to close at 10.74 cents/lb while the outer months gained 2 to 5 points.

Traders said further gains could prove difficult and speculators remained wary of adding to their already hefty long positions. Traders estimated that speculators could be net long of up to 30,000 lots on the May contract, which carried a total open interest of 73,206 as of Thursday's close.

INDIA - Indian sugar production during October 1/February 15, 1996/96 totalled 7.030 million tonnes, white value, 11 percent less than the 7.857 million tonnes produced in the same period in 1995/96. However, opening stocks of 7.902 million tonnes were significantly above last year's level of 5.598 million tonnes so that total availability this season of 14.932 million tonnes is significantly up on last year's figure of 13.455 million tonnes. Offtake till February 15 reached 5.296 million tonnes, nearly 8 percent up on last year. Exports remain sluggish and reached only 286,000 tonnes during October 1/January 15 compared to 357,000 tonnes the same period in 1995/96.

EGYPT - Egypt could end up delaying some of its recent raw sugar purchases until the second half of 1997, due to port congestion, London trade sources said. However, the quantity of sugar involved is thought to be limited. The country gets most of its sugar from Cuba and Brazil. Cuba shipped 165,693 tonnes of raw sugar to Egypt in 1995, down from 301,100 tonnes the previous year. Brazil shipped 16,214 tonnes of raw sugar in 1996 to Egypt, down from 107,900 tonnes in 1995 and 13,810 tonnes in 1994. White sugar shipments in 1996 fell to 318,933 tonnes, down from 601,776 tonnes the previous year but up from the 86,413 tonnes shipped in 1994.

JAPAN - Japan imported 113,291 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in January 1997, 28 percent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996/97 (October) to 618,142 tonnes which compares to 609,563 tonnes the same period in 1995/96. Total imports in crop year 1995/96 (October/September) reached 1.681 million tonnes, down from 1.716 million tonnes the previous year and 1.704 million tonnes in 1993/94. Main countries of origin for raw sugar in October/January 1996/97 were South Africa (114,542 vs 129,768 tonnes), Thailand (91,850 vs 104,485 tonnes) and Australia (354,540 vs 373,334 tonnes).
